title: Festschriften
summary: Festschriften receive headings for their subject matter as a whole, normally without form subdivision (--Addresses, essays, lectures was discontinued in 1986), with --Congresses if the work results from a congress. The honoree is assigned only if more than 20% of the work is about them, with --Bibliography if a bibliography of the honoree exceeds 20%. LC catalogers (2026) add LCGFT Festschriften.
validation_rules: Assign headings covering the subject matter of the festschrift as a whole, normally without a form subdivision. (H 1600 sec. D)
The subdivision `--Addresses, essays, lectures` was discontinued in 1986; do not use it. (H 1600 sec. D)
If the festschrift results from a congress held in honor of the person, society, etc., use the form subdivision `--Congresses`. (H 1600 sec. D)
Assign a heading for the honoree (person or corporate body) only if more than 20% of the work is about the honoree. (H 1600 sec. E)
If a bibliography relating to the honoree is more than 20% of the work, assign `[honoree]--Bibliography`. (H 1600 sec. E)

[LC practice] Assign topical headings per standard practice and LCGFT `Festschriften` (`655 #7 $a Festschriften. $2 lcgft`); for an honoree bibliography over 20%, assign the honoree's name without `--Bibliography` and LCGFT `Bibliographies`. (H 1600 sec. D, E)

sections.heading: A. Background
sections.text:
A festschrift is a complimentary or memorial publication usually in the form of a collection of essays, addresses, or biographical, bibliographical, scientific, or other contributions, often embodying the results of research, issued in honor of a person, an institution, or a society, usually on the occasion of an anniversary celebration. This instruction sheet provides guidelines for assigning subject headings to festschriften.

LC practice: As stated in H 1075, LC catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT), e.g. *Textbooks*. To replace a form subdivision that includes a demographic group, also assign Library of Congress Demographic Groups Terms (LCDGT) to bring out the audience of the resource being cataloged, e.g. *German speakers* or *Arabic, Students of*.

sections.heading: B. Recent revisions
sections.text: 2026-07: Updated template. Added instructions related to LCGFT implementation.

sections.heading: C. Definitions
sections.text: Festschrift: complimentary or memorial publication usually in the form of a collection of essays, addresses, or biographical, bibliographical, scientific, or other contributions, often embodying the results of research, issued in honor of a person, an institution, or a society, usually on the occasion of an anniversary celebration

sections.heading: D. Topic
sections.text:
Assign a heading or headings to cover the subject matter of the festschrift as a whole, normally without form subdivision. (The subdivision *--Addresses, essays, lectures*, formerly used for this type of material, was discontinued in 1986.)

If the work is the result of a congress held in honor of the person, society, etc., use the form subdivision *--Congresses*.

LC practice: Assign heading(s) for the topic(s) covered in the festschrift, following standard practices. Assign LCGFT appropriate to the form and/or genre of the resource in hand, e.g. LCGFT *Festschriften*.

Examples:

```
Title: Africa in the long run : festschrift in the honour of Professor Arvi Hurskainen.
600 10 $a Hurskainen, Arvi.
650 #0 $a Ethnology $z Africa
650 #0 $a Anthropological linguistics $z Africa.
650 #0 $a African languages $x Research
651 #0 $a Africa $x Social life and customs.
LC practice:
No change of subject headings.
655 #7 $a Festschriften. $2 lcgft
```

sections.heading: E. Honoree(s)
sections.text:
Assign a heading for the name of the person or corporate body in whose honor the publication is issued only if more than 20% of the work is about the person or corporate body.

If the work contains a bibliography relating to the honoree which is more than 20% of the work, assign the name of the honoree with the subdivision *--Bibliography*.

LC practice: If the work contains a bibliography relating to the honoree which is more than 20% of the work, assign the name of the honoree as a subject heading. Assign LCGFT appropriate to the form and/or genre of the resource in hand, e.g. LCGFT *Bibliographies*.
